title: CPI vs. WPI Inflation Indices & Food Inflation Dynamics
summary: Consumer Price Index (CPI) measures retail buyer price changes across 2012 weights, while Wholesale Price Index (WPI) measures producer bulk transaction prices.

blocks.title: First-Principles Core Truth
blocks.summary: Consumer Price Index (CPI) measures retail buyer price changes across 2012 weights, while Wholesale Price Index (WPI) measures producer bulk transaction prices.

blocks.content: 1. Consumer Price Index (CPI): Measures price changes at retail level paid by ultimate consumers. Base year: **2012=100**. Released monthly by **NSO (MoSPI)**.
2. Wholesale Price Index (WPI): Measures price changes at wholesale/producer bulk transaction level. Base year: **2011-12=100**. Released monthly by **Office of Economic Adviser (DPIIT)**.
3. Food Weightage Divergence: CPI Combined has a massive **45.86% weight for Food & Beverages**. WPI has only **24.38% weight for Food Items**.
4. Services Inclusion: Services (Housing, Medical, Education, Transport) are **INCLUDED in CPI**, but **EXCLUDED from WPI** (WPI covers goods only!).

blocks.text:
⚡ 1. CPI vs. WPI Comprehensive Feature Matrix
| Parameter | Consumer Price Index (CPI Combined) | Wholesale Price Index (WPI) |
|---|---|---|
| **Level of Measurement** | Retail consumer price level | Wholesale / First point of bulk sale |
| **Publishing Agency** | National Sample Survey Office (NSO), MoSPI | Office of Economic Adviser, DPIIT (Min of Commerce) |
| **Current Base Year** | **2012 = 100** | **2011-12 = 100** |
| **Food Basket Weight** | **45.86%** (High sensitivity to food prices) | **24.38%** (Combined Food Index) |
| **Manufactured Goods Weight**| 23.80% | **64.23%** (Dominant sector in WPI) |
| **Services Sector** | **INCLUDED** (Housing 10.07%, Health, Transport) | **EXCLUDED** (Measures goods only) |
| **RBI Monetary Anchor** | **Primary Anchor** for Flexible Inflation Targeting (4%±2%) | Secondary indicator for producer margins |

📖 2. 4 Sub-Types of Consumer Price Index (CPI) in India
1. **CPI (Rural, Urban, Combined):** Base 2012=100, published by NSO (MoSPI).
2. **CPI for Agricultural Laborers (CPI-AL):** Base 1986-87=100, published by **Labour Bureau (Ministry of Labour & Employment)**. Used for updating minimum wages in farming.
3. **CPI for Rural Laborers (CPI-RL):** Base 1986-87=100, published by Labour Bureau.
4. **CPI for Industrial Workers (CPI-IW):** Base **2016=100**, published by Labour Bureau. Used for calculating **Dearness Allowance (DA)** of central government employees!

⚖️ 3. Common Prelims & Mains Traps
- ⚠️ **Exam Trap 1:** WPI does NOT measure price changes for Services (banking, software, health)! Only CPI includes Services.
- ⚠️ **Exam Trap 2:** RBI switched its monetary anchor from WPI to **CPI Combined** in 2014 based on Urjit Patel Committee recommendations.

blocks.content:
#### Tier 1 — Recall MCQ
**Q:** Which index is published by the Labour Bureau (Ministry of Labour & Employment) and used to determine Dearness Allowance (DA) for central government employees?  
(A) CPI Combined (NSO)  
(B) CPI for Industrial Workers (CPI-IW)  
(C) Wholesale Price Index (WPI)  
(D) GDP Deflator  
**Answer: — CPI-IW (Base 2016) is published by Labour Bureau for DA calculation.

#### Tier 2 — Applied Scenario
**Scenario:** Agricultural drought causes a sharp 30% increase in vegetable prices while global manufacturing metal prices fall by 15%. Explain why CPI inflation spikes while WPI inflation drops.  
**Resolution:** Food weight in CPI is **45.86%** (dominating retail CPI upwards), whereas Manufactured goods weight in WPI is **64.23%** (pulling wholesale WPI downwards).

#### Tier 3 — Mains Descriptive Prompt
*'Compare the structural weightage and coverage of CPI and WPI in India. Why did RBI select CPI Combined as its policy anchor under Flexible Inflation Targeting?'*

🎯 Exam Angle → 🔥 HIGH — CPI vs WPI Traps: (1) CPI covers Goods & Services (Base 2012=100, NSO); WPI covers ONLY Goods (Base 2011-12=100, DPIIT/MoCI); (2) Food weight in CPI is ~45.86% vs ~24.38% in WPI; (3) Headline inflation is CPI Combined; Core inflation is CPI excluding Food and Fuel.
